messages:
sarah: noticing a perf regression on canary today, looks like throughput drops when KV hit rate dips under 70% :thinking_face:
kevin: saw that too, stacktrace points to kernel selection doing a fallthrough to the slower aten path while KV eviction churn is high
lucas: curious — are we seeing larger avg sequence lengths or more small sequences that bypass caching?
sarah: small sequences mostly, but a few long tails. kv-miss rate spike correlates with increased mem pressure and a recompile fallback to safe kernels
maria: uploaded a flamegraph from the canary run: https://artifacts/redwood/canary/3730102023/flame.svg — kernel_select and kv_lookup are spiking together
kevin: here are the hotlines from perf probe (simplified):
```
kernel_select() -> aten_gpt_fast (17%), aten_safe_fallback (63%)
kv_lookup() -> miss_rate 32% -> mem_gc 1.2s
batch_form() -> avg_batch_tokens 42 -> token_budget_hit 88%
```
lucas: so when kv pressure climbs we end up picking aten_safe_fallback which increases per-token latency and reduces batch packing efficiency, causing more pressure -> cycle
sarah: yeah, it's a feedback loop. current batch admission doesn't account for cache eviction cost. we need an oom-avoidance heuristic that biases against aggressive batching when predicted cache delta > threshold
maria: tried a quick patch locally: "elastic-token-cushion" — adds a cushion token budget proportional to estimated cache-fragmentation. config snippet:
```
batcher:
  token_cushion: dynamic
  cushion_fn: max(ceil(0.1 * predicted_kv_eviction_tokens), 4)
  kernel_penalty: { safe_fallback: 1.4 }
```
kevin: experiment results on machine with 4x A100: baseline p99 latency 210ms, patch p99 185ms under mixed workload (50/50 short/long), throughput +6% and peak mem-gc events down by 40%
lucas: nice. what's the downside? does it reduce average utilization?
maria: small utilization drop for extremely stable cached workloads (~2-3%) but eliminates the regression corner when cache misses spike. also kernel route stability improved (less recompile churn)
sarah: we should also try a kernel-selection bias: when predicted_kv_eviction_tokens > X, prefer kernel that tolerates sparse KV (favors "kv-friendly" path), even if slightly higher core latency — reduces GC-induced tail spikes
kevin: added a flag to runtime: `--prefer-kv-friendly` and a telemetry tag. ran 10k requests canary: errors 0, p99 down vs baseline, cpu utilization +1%, memory pause rate -0.6/min
infra-bot: canary report uploaded: https://canary-reports/redwood/3730102023 — status: PASS with the elastic-token-cushion heuristic enabled :white_check_mark:
sarah: awesome. next steps: 1) bake heuristic into batcher + opt-out flag, 2) add telemetry for predicted_kv_eviction_tokens and kernel_route_choice, 3) run a 24h canary across 3 regions to catch long-tail effects
lucas: I'll sketch a proposal for admission policy change and a small smoke test harness for eviction-surge injection
maria: I'll PR the patch and include perf harness results + flamegraph comparisons
kevin: leaving a note: need to ensure cushion math uses live KV slab stats (not laggy aggregator), otherwise we'll oscillate
sarah: agreed. keep cushion conservative initially (low alpha). good job team :rocket:
